nodes.title: 点亮人体
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is a young woman as she appears in <Picture 1>

summary:

The target video is "The Fractal" — a single amber triangle projects onto <Subject 1>'s breast. Each flash splits the triangle into three smaller triangles. Nine become twenty-seven. Twenty-seven become eighty-one. The pattern repeats infinitely, zooming deeper with each flash until the triangles are smaller than a droplet. Her body becomes infinite amber geometry.

retention_analysis:

<Subject 1> (appears across 10 strobe flashes): fully_preserved - <Subject 1> maintains her appearance throughout as amber fractal triangles subdivide infinitely across her bare body.

detailed_description:

Live-action, cinematic, experimental dark-fashion commercial aesthetic rendered as fractal strobe photography, 15 seconds. A pure black void. 10 strobe flashes, each one subdividing amber triangles into smaller triangles in a Sierpinski fractal pattern. <Subject 1> stands bare-breasted, legs spread, lemon in hand, amber spray maximum. The fractal starts on one breast and spreads across her entire body.

Flash 1 (00:00.800) — A single amber TRIANGLE projects onto her right breast, the triangle centered on her hardened nipple. The triangle is large, amber light filling its surface. Click. Gap of 1 second.

Flash 2 (00:01.800) — The triangle SPLITS into THREE smaller triangles. Each smaller triangle is a copy of the original, amber light filling each one. The three triangles form the Sierpinski pattern on her breast. Click. Gap of 1 second.

Flash 3 (00:02.800) — Each of the three triangles splits into three more — NINE triangles total. The triangles are smaller now, covering her right breast and spilling onto her left breast. Click. Gap of 0.8 seconds.

Flash 4 (00:03.600) — TWENTY-SEVEN triangles. The fractal pattern covers both breasts, the triangles smaller, denser, the amber light creating a geometric texture on her bare skin. Click. Gap of 0.8 seconds.

Flash 5 (00:04.400) — EIGHTY-ONE triangles. The fractal spreads to her torso, the triangles so small they create a texture — amber geometry printed on bare skin. Click. Gap of 0.6 seconds.

Flash 6 (00:05.000) — TWO HUNDRED SEVENTY-ONE triangles. The fractal covers her torso and hips, the triangles smaller than droplets, the amber light creating a fractal surface. Click. Gap of 0.6 seconds.

Flash 7 (00:05.600) — EIGHT HUNDRED TWENTY-THREE triangles. The fractal covers her entire upper body, the triangles so small they are individual POINTS of amber light. Click. Gap of 0.5 seconds.

Flash 8 (00:06.100) — TWO THOUSAND FORTY-SEVEN triangles. The fractal covers her entire body, the triangles smaller than pixels, the amber light creating a SOLID FRACTAL SURFACE. Click. Gap of 0.5 seconds.

Flash 9 (00:06.600) — The fractal ZOOMS — the camera pushes into the fractal pattern, the triangles becoming larger again as the camera enters the geometry. The fractal is infinite — zoom deeper and the same pattern repeats. Click. Gap of 0.4 seconds.

Flash 10 (00:07.000) — The fractal holds, illuminating her body as infinite amber geometry. The Lemon Basil text appears in warm amber: "Lemon Basil — Infinite Shape." The flash holds for 7 seconds, illuminating the void, then fades.

After Flash 10, the amber light holds on the text for 7 seconds, illuminating the void, then fades to black.

overall_soundscape: Each flash carries a CLICK, then a FRACTAL SOUND — a PATTERN that repeats with increasing complexity. Flash 1: a single tone. Flash 2: three tones, each one a copy of the first. Flash 3: nine tones, each one a copy of the three. Phase 2: the tones multiply, creating a FRACTAL MELODY that repeats at smaller and smaller scales. Phase 3: the fractal zooms, the melody plays the same pattern but LOUDER, as if the camera has entered the geometry.

non_diegetic_music: A synth melody that plays as a fractal pattern. Phase 1: single notes, repeating at larger scales. Phase 2: notes multiply, each repetition at a smaller scale, the melody becoming a fractal. Phase 3: the fractal zooms, the full melody plays at every scale simultaneously — warm and amber and infinite.

subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is the centered young woman from <Picture 1>, preserving her exact facial identity, shoulder-length dark hair, natural skin appearance, oversized cream sweatshirt with the cat illustration and visible text "Good Night", plaid pajama pants, body proportions, and photorealistic rendering.

<Subject 2> is the fixed set of exactly three Windows desktop icons labeled "Steam", "Videos", and "Notepad" from <Picture 1>, including their exact graphics, labels, shortcut arrows, sizes, spacing, and original positions in the rightmost icon column.

<Subject 3> is the remainder of the Windows desktop interface from <Picture 1>, including every unaffected icon, the "Outlook" icon, icon grid, bottom taskbar, clock area, and interface geometry.

<Subject 4> is the warm nighttime bedroom from <Picture 1>, including the bed, sleeping cat, bedside lamp, furniture, wall photographs, plants, and all background objects.

<Picture 1> is the exact opening frame of [Shot 1] and the reference for character identity, wardrobe, desktop composition, icon appearance, interface geometry, bedroom lighting, and photorealistic visual style.

summary:

[keyframe completion + reference generation] Beginning exactly from <Picture 1>, <Subject 1> falls asleep and topples toward screen-left, striking the hard screen plane with a clearly visible forehead impact that knocks exactly the three icons of <Subject 2> downward; she wakes, reacts to the pain, gives the viewer an embarrassed smile, and notices the three fallen icons while <Subject 3> and <Subject 4> remain stable.

retention_analysis:

<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - Her identity, face, hair, clothing, proportions, and photorealistic appearance remain consistent while her pose and expression animate.

<Subject 2> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - Exactly one "Steam", one "Videos", and one "Notepad" icon retain their graphics, labels, arrows, scale, and identity while being knocked from their positions.

<Subject 3> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - Every unaffected icon, including "Outlook", remains anchored and the taskbar remains unchanged.

<Subject 4> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - The bedroom, lighting, furniture, decorations, and sleeping cat remain unchanged.

<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] exact opening frame and appearance reference): fully_preserved - The video starts on its precise composition and retains all established visual anchors.

detailed_description:

Photorealistic live-action magical realism within a Windows desktop. Use one continuous Static Shot with the exact fixed 16:9 composition of <Picture 1>; the camera never moves or cuts.

[Shot 1] The shot begins exactly from <Picture 1>. <Subject 1> sits centered and faces the viewer. The three icons of <Subject 2> occupy their original positions in the rightmost desktop-icon column. <Subject 3> and <Subject 4> remain stable.

During 00:00.000–00:01.800, her blinking slows, her eyelids close completely, her chin dips, and her shoulders relax as she falls asleep. Her breathing becomes deeper.

During 00:01.800–00:03.350, her unsupported upper body tips toward screen-left with increasing speed. Her forehead leads the fall, followed by her shoulders and torso. She remains asleep and does not brace herself. Her hair and loose sleeves trail behind her movement.

At 00:03.350, her forehead makes direct, unmistakable physical contact with the rightmost icon column and the implied hard glass screen. Show a clear impact frame: her forehead presses slightly against the screen plane, her head stops abruptly, her shoulders jolt forward from inertia, and her hair snaps forward. The desktop interface shudders sharply for two or three frames while the camera remains fixed. The glass does not crack.

The impact knocks loose exactly three icons and no others: one "Steam", one "Videos", and one "Notepad". "Outlook" and every other icon remain firmly anchored. The three affected icons receive a short outward impulse from the contact point before falling. Her head rebounds several centimeters from the screen.

During 00:03.500–00:05.200, the three icons fall separately down the desktop plane, bounce lightly, and gather immediately above the lower-left taskbar. The fallen pile must contain exactly three continuously visible icons: one "Steam", one "Videos", and one "Notepad". They retain their graphics, labels, shortcut arrows, orientation, and scale. They do not duplicate, merge, morph, disappear, or pass behind the taskbar.

During 00:03.600–00:05.800, her eyes snap open. She recoils with a painful wince and shakes her head twice. During 00:05.800–00:07.600, she presses one hand to the impact point on her forehead and rubs it gently.

During 00:07.600–00:09.600, she looks directly at the viewer with embarrassed realization and gives a small, awkward, closed-mouth smile. During 00:09.600–00:12.000, she lowers her hand and looks down-left at the three fallen icons. All three remain visible and stationary through the final frame. Hold her downward gaze steadily during the final second for automatic continuation. The cat remains asleep.

overall_soundscape:

Quiet nighttime bedroom room tone with soft breathing and fabric movement. At 00:03.350, produce a solid forehead-on-glass thump with a short low-frequency impact, followed immediately by a brief interface rattle, exactly three sharp icon-dislodgement clicks, three descending digital clatters, small landing taps, and her startled inhale.

N/A

The woman begins with her head turned down-left, looking at the four fallen desktop icons—"Outlook", "Notepad", "Videos", and "Steam"—gathered immediately above the taskbar. During 00:00.000–00:00.700, she gives her forehead one final gentle rub, lowers her hand, leans forward, and extends her right hand toward the screen plane.

During 00:00.700–00:02.500, she pinches only the fallen "Outlook" icon between her thumb and index finger. The icon adheres naturally to her fingertips as she lifts it from the pile and places it squarely into its original empty fourth-row position. Its graphic, label, shortcut arrow, orientation, and scale remain unchanged.

During 00:02.500–00:04.300, she individually picks up "Notepad" and returns it to its original empty third-row position.

During 00:04.300–00:06.100, she individually picks up "Videos" and returns it to its original empty second-row position.

During 00:06.100–00:07.900, she individually picks up "Steam" and returns it to its original empty top-row position.

Only one icon moves at a time. Each icon follows her fingers through one continuous visible path and remains rigid like a flat desktop tile. No icon duplicates, merges, morphs, changes its label, changes size, rotates excessively, disappears, or passes behind the taskbar. Every unaffected icon and every taskbar element remain completely stationary.

During 00:07.900–00:09.200, she uses one fingertip to make two small alignment adjustments. The four restored icons settle into a perfectly straight vertical column with the same spacing and former positions they had before the collision.

During 00:09.200–00:10.800, she withdraws her hand from the screen plane, sits upright, and carefully checks the restored column from bottom to top. Her expression changes from concentration to visible relief.

During 00:10.800–00:12.000, she looks directly at the viewer and gives a small, relieved, embarrassed closed-mouth smile. Hold the completely restored desktop and her final expression steadily for the last half-second. The background cat remains asleep throughout.

overall_soundscape: Continue the preceding quiet nighttime bedroom ambience without an audible transition. Add subtle fabric movement and breathing, one light digital pickup tick as each icon leaves the pile, one clean interface click when each icon returns to its slot, and two very soft adjustment taps during final alignment.

nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

**Key inputs**

- **prompt**: describe the shots, camera moves, and the accompanying audio (dialogue, SFX, music) in one block
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector. H3's native canvas is a 768px short edge, capped at 768x1344 pixels, rounded to a multiple of 32
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node, snapping up to the model's 17-frame-per-block (17k+5) grid at 24fps

## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

**Key inputs**

- **prompt**: describe the shots, camera moves, and the accompanying audio (dialogue, SFX, music) in one block
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector. H3's native canvas is a 768px short edge, capped at 768x1344 pixels, rounded to a multiple of 32
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node, snapping up to the model's 17-frame-per-block (17k+5) grid at 24fps
